name: Addis Ababa University
distanceNote: Inside the capital, but which campus you actually live near depends entirely on your department.
campuses: Sidist Kilo is the old heart of the university and where most humanities and social science students spend their days, walking distance from the John F. Kennedy Library. Arat Kilo is a short walk from there and holds natural and computational sciences. 5 Kilo, home to AAiT, feels like its own university within the university, engineering students there rarely mix much with the rest of campus. Tikur Anbessa is where health science students end up living once clinical years start, attached to the hospital itself. Business and economics sit closer to the Piassa side of town. If you get placed at Bishoftu for veterinary medicine, you are effectively not in Addis anymore, that is a 45 minute plus drive and a genuinely different daily life.
knownFor: Water resource management — national reference programs, not just a course name on a brochure
Medical and health sciences anchored at Tikur Anbessa; clinical years are hospital life, not campus life

whatToExpect: The size is the first shock. Classes in first year general courses can run into the hundreds, and lecturers will not know your name unless you make a point of being known.

Attendance policy is taken seriously here more than students expect. Miss too many sessions in a course and you can be barred from sitting the final exam entirely, this is not a rumor, it happens every semester to students who assumed lecture was optional.

The academic dismissal system runs on GPA, and it is strict. Fall below the cutoff for your program two semesters running and you can be dismissed regardless of how much you have already invested. Nobody explains this clearly during orientation, so ask your department secretary directly what your program's cutoff actually is.

Dorm life is crowded. Expect to share a room built for two with one or two more people than that, especially in your first year. Water gets cut without warning often enough that keeping a filled jerrycan is just normal life, not paranoia.
Cafeteria food is filling but repetitive, most students who can afford it supplement with food from small shops just outside campus gates within the first month.

The registrar and administrative offices move slowly. A transcript correction or a missing grade can take weeks of follow up, bring printed copies of everything and keep them, do not assume a problem was fixed just because someone said it would be.

Because the campus is spread across a real city, a huge amount of unofficial learning happens through senior students. Find someone a year or two ahead in your specific department in your first two weeks, they will save you more time than any orientation session.
5 Kilo teaches software, electrical, biomedical, mechanical, civil, and chemical engineering, AAU is one of the few universities in the country teaching biomedical engineering at all
4 Kilo, a separate site from 5 Kilo despite both sounding like general engineering, teaches computer science and computer engineering specifically

Sefere Selam is where nursing and related health fields study for their first years before moving to Tikur Anbessa for third year and clinical work, so your early health science years likely will not be at the hospital campus at all
18 Mazoria handles other allied health fields, a separate identity again from Sefere Selam and Tikur Anbessa
Lideta is where architecture, construction, and urban planning live, distinct from the engineering fields at 5 Kilo
Mexico campus is where commerce, marketing, business administration, and management are taught, separate from both the humanities at Sidist Kilo and the engineering campuses
tips: If you are in AAiT, arrive already comfortable with your math fundamentals, the pace assumes you are, and the first semester does not slow down for people who are still catching up.

If you are heading into health sciences, understand now that once clinical rotations begin your schedule stops being your own, hospital hours do not care about exam schedules for your other remaining courses.
Introduce yourself to your department secretary early and learn their name. They control far more of your daily reality, registration issues, room changes, missing documents, than any professor does.
Keep every stamped document the university gives you, admission letter, ID, grade reports, in a folder you control. Offices lose paperwork here more often than students expect.

Join one club or student association in your first month even if you are shy. AAU is large enough that it is easy to become anonymous, and the students who struggle most socially are usually the ones who never attached themselves to a smaller group inside the bigger one.
Ask specifically which numbered campus, not just 'AAiT' as a general name, your exact engineering field is taught at, since 4 Kilo and 5 Kilo are different sites teaching different things
studentFit: AAU rewards students who can be self reliant inside a large, sometimes impersonal system. You will need to advocate for yourself with administration, keep track of your own deadlines and GPA standing, and build your own smaller community inside a very large one. If you need a lot of individual attention from instructors or a tightly held hand through bureaucracy, the size here will wear on you. If you can handle being one of many while still finding your footing, very few places in the country will hand you more doors to walk through afterward.
